claims.text: An Al-containing Co-Cr-Fe-Ni high-entropy alloy provides superior elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion resistance compared with traditional structural alloys.
The Al-containing Co-Cr-Fe-Ni alloy forms a stable protective oxide layer under elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion conditions.
The protective oxide layer is self-healing.
The proposed initial material is a solution-annealed AlxCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy.
The solution-annealed alloy has a homogeneous multiphase microstructure.
The relevant operating-temperature range is approximately 600–800 °C.
Simultaneous sliding wear and exposure to a chemically aggressive medium represent the proposed tribo-corrosion conditions.
Tribo-corrosion exposure produces a continuous and adherent passive oxide layer on the alloy surface.
The surface oxide layer is enriched in Al2O3 and Cr2O3.
The presence of multiple principal elements slows diffusion in the alloy.
The presence of multiple principal elements promotes uniform elemental distribution.
Slower diffusion and uniform elemental distribution enhance the formation and stability of protective oxide scales.
The protective oxide scales reduce chemical attack by acting as a surface barrier.
The protective oxide scales reduce mechanical erosion during tribo-corrosion.
The alloy will exhibit a lower wear rate than stainless steel under identical high-temperature tribo-corrosion conditions.
The alloy will exhibit less corrosion degradation than stainless steel under identical high-temperature tribo-corrosion conditions.
Performance improvement may be lost above the temperature regime that favors stable oxide formation.
Aggressive environmental species may destabilize the protective oxide layer and limit performance.
